behaviour: C1: leftGroupTombstones.ts: idb-keyval store few-left-groups/tombstones, key groupId, value {groupId, leftAt}; put, delete, list (malformed rows ignored), listLeftGroupIds, clearAll. Local-only, never published, never exported in the backup.
C2: leaveGroupImpl writes the tombstone BEFORE removeGroupFromStorage (a failed write is warned and never skips the purge). The purge and reloadGroups stay immediate and never wait on the network.

C3: With a kind-9 departure announcement in flight, the MLS-state destroy runs only after that send resolves, rejects, or LEAVE_DESTROY_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS (5 s) passes, without being awaited by leaveGroupImpl; then the tombstone is deleted. With no send (abandon/last member, no MLS group, no identity) the destroy runs inline before reloadGroups. A failed destroy is warned, keeps the tombstone, and never throws or rejects unhandled.

C4: The destroy is welcomeSubscription.destroyLeftGroupState: under withGroupJoinLock(groupId); overlay present -> 'rejoined' (nothing destroyed); no MLS state -> 'absent'; else marmotClient.groups.destroy(groupId) (local-only) -> 'destroyed'.

C5: Startup sweep sweepLeftGroups runs in loadGroupsAndReconcileInvitations after groups.loadAll() and before dropInvitationsForJoinedGroups (skipped when loadAll fails). For each tombstone it calls destroyLeftGroupState and drops the tombstone; a failure keeps that tombstone (retried next start) and never blocks startup. MLS state without a tombstone is never touched; tombstone + overlay never destroys MLS state (the stale tombstone is dropped so the live group's state is backed up again).
C6: joinIdempotent's orphan branch deletes the tombstone after its destroy (a delete failure is warned and does not fail the accept).
C7: collectBackupPayload exports MLS state only for keys that are overlay group ids not in the tombstone set. Restore is unchanged (add/update-only).
C8: clearAllGroupData clears the tombstone store.
C9: Privacy invariant untouched: destroy is local, no new publishes.
non_goals: Part 2 of the design (self-eviction detection, re-invite after eviction).
Describing what an evicted member sees.
